validated_results.title: [Primary prevention of bladder cancer. What's new?].
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review summarizing published epidemiological findings on primary prevention of bladder cancer, including a passing mention of a yogurt study, rather than original human data.

validated_results.title: Re-assessment of the influence of polymorphisms of phase-II metabolic enzymes on renal cell cancer risk of trichloroethylene-exposed workers.
validated_results.journal: International archives of occupational and environmental health
validated_results.reason: The study examines occupational trichloroethylene exposure and glutathione S-transferase gene polymorphisms, not nutritional glutathione exposure.

validated_results.title: Re-assessment of the influence of polymorphisms of phase-II metabolic enzymes on renal cell cancer risk of trichloroethylene-exposed workers.
validated_results.journal: International archives of occupational and environmental health
validated_results.reason: Renal cell cancer risk is analyzed by GSTT1/GSTM1/GSTP1/NAT2 genotype among trichloroethylene-exposed workers, with no nutritional glutathione exposure assessed.

validated_results.title: Probucol modulates iron nitrilotriacetate (Fe-NTA)-dependent renal carcinogenesis and hyperproliferative response: diminution of oxidative stress.
validated_results.reason: Probucol antioxidant supplementation and Fe-NTA renal tumor incidence were studied exclusively in mice.

validated_results.title: Probucol modulates iron nitrilotriacetate (Fe-NTA)-dependent renal carcinogenesis and hyperproliferative response: diminution of oxidative stress.
validated_results.reason: Iron nitrilotriacetate-induced renal carcinogenesis was evaluated only in an experimental mouse model, not in humans.

validated_results.title: Alcohol intake and renal cell cancer in a pooled analysis of 12 prospective studies.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: Pooled analysis of 12 prospective cohorts reporting dietary alcohol intake and incident renal cell cancer risk with a multivariable pooled relative risk.

sample_size.excerpt: An inverse association between alcohol intake and risk of renal cell cancer has been suggested in a few prospective studies, but each of these studies included a small number of cases. We performed a pooled analysis of 12 prospective studies that included 530,469 women and 229,575 men with maximum follow-up times of 7-20 years.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 530469 + 229575 = 760044

cases.excerpt: A total of 1430 (711 women and 719 men) cases of incident renal cell cancer were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with nondrinking, alcohol consumption (> or = 15 g/day, equivalent to slightly more than one alcoholic drink per day) was associated with a decreased risk of renal cell cancer (pooled multivariable RR = 0.72, 95% confidence interval = 0.60 to 0.86; P(trend)<.001); statistically significant inverse trends with increasing intake were seen in both women and men.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared with nondrinking, alcohol consumption (> or = 15 g/day, equivalent to slightly more than one alcoholic drink per day) was associated with a decreased risk of renal cell cancer (pooled multivariable RR = 0.72, 95% confidence interval = 0.60 to 0.86; P(trend)<.001); statistically significant inverse trends with increasing intake were seen in both women and men.

sample_size.excerpt: Therefore, we investigated in depth the topic of fibres and RCC, using data from a multicenter case-control study conducted in Italy from 1992 to 2004, including 767 cases with incident, histologically confirmed RCC and 1,534 controls admitted to the same network of hospitals as cases with acute nonmalignant conditions.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 767 + 1534 = 2301

cases.excerpt: Therefore, we investigated in depth the topic of fibres and RCC, using data from a multicenter case-control study conducted in Italy from 1992 to 2004, including 767 cases with incident, histologically confirmed RCC and 1,534 controls admitted to the same network of hospitals as cases with acute nonmalignant conditions.

effect_size.excerpt: The continuous OR for an increase in intake equal to the difference between the 80th and the 20th percentile were 0.94 (95% CI: 0.82-1.08) for total dietary fibre, 0.98 (95% CI: 0.85-1.13) for soluble noncellulose polysaccharides, 0.92 (95% CI: 0.80-1.05) for total insoluble fibre, 0.90 (95% CI: 0.78-1.04) for cellulose, 0.95 (95% CI: 0.84-1.06) for insoluble noncellulose polysaccharides and 1.06 (95% CI: 0.93-1.21) for lignin. With reference to the sources of fibre, we found an inverse association with vegetable fibre (OR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.73-0.97), but no association with fruit (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.86-1.12) and grain fibre (OR = 1.05, 95% CI: 0.95-1.15).
